solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping); the blog's combined-key rows for 10/26/11A, 13/28A and 25/22/9D each printed only the leading light's word (LEAD, TALK, WITH) and dropped the trailing words their own members' rows already gave correctly (UP THE GARDEN PATH, INTO, OPEN ARMS) — corrected to the full phrases

clue.text: Piss over Mail's Andrew?

indicators.note: one thing laid over another covers it on both sides, so the drink wraps around the paper

blocks.note: piss is British slang for weak or poor beer
the mail is the post in British usage

explanation.surface: A crude insult aimed at a Daily Mail columnist called Andrew.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mail reads as the Daily Mail newspaper, but it is just the post; Andrew is not a journalist but the saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Andrew was one of the twelve disciples chosen by Jesus, so he is an example of the group.

clue.text: Gather it's a petition against Trump at the outset

indicators.note: the outset is the very start, so only the opening letter of Trump is wanted

blocks.note: a plea is an appeal or petition
the first letter of Trump

explanation.surface: Collecting signatures on a petition opposing Trump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Against' only places one piece next to the other here.
explanation.definitionFit: In sewing, to pleat cloth is to fold or gather it into regular tucks.

clue.text: Faction put forward a motion – appreciated by armchair scoffer?

blocks.note: a side is a faction or party in a dispute
to table a motion is to put it forward for debate

explanation.surface: A political group proposes a motion that a lazy armchair critic applauds.
explanation.walkthrough: The scoffer seems to mock from the armchair, but here he scoffs food, wanting a surface beside him for snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A small table beside an armchair holds plates and drinks for someone eating while seated.

clue.text: Roger to get this, say, stuck in fan

indicators.note: something stuck in something else sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: say means for example, abbreviated e.g.
a fan or enthusiast is a lover of something

explanation.surface: Seems to describe Roger Federer getting a shot past a fan.
explanation.walkthrough: Roger is British slang for having sex, and a legover is British slang for an act of sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wanting to roger is after a sexual encounter, which British slang calls a legover.

clue.text: Used heroin to ensnare state leader – but not in deep water

indicators.note: drugs that are used or abused are messed about with, so the letters get rearranged
a leader comes at the front, so only the first letter of state counts
to ensnare is to trap something inside, so one piece is caught within another

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the first letter of state

explanation.surface: A drug sting where heroin is used to trap a politician, who is not yet in serious trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not in deep water' sounds like escaping trouble, but it is literal: close to the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Waters near the coast are shallow compared with the open ocean, so close-to-land fishing or sailing is described this way.

clue.text: New leader, new Tory takes measure: Exit only?

indicators.note: the leader is at the head, so only the first letter of New is taken
something made new is remade, so the letters of Tory are rearranged
taking something in means holding it, so the rearranged word swallows the measure

blocks.note: first letter of New
taken as written, to be rearranged
an en is a printer's unit of measure

explanation.surface: A new Conservative leader takes action on Brexit, suggesting leaving but nothing coming in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exit only' hints at Brexit and immigration, but it is just a sign on a door.
explanation.definitionFit: A door marked for leaving only forbids people from coming in that way, which is what this sign announces.

clue.text: Bound to have sex and then withdraw

blocks.note: to bound is to hop or leap
it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: A crude account of a quick sexual encounter followed by withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdraw' seems to continue the sex, but it means simply leave; hop it is British slang for go away.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal British command to clear off means leaving a place, the same as departing or retreating.

clue.text: Simon, musically, has rotten run through

blocks.note: Sir Simon Rattle is a famous British conductor
food that has gone rotten is off

explanation.surface: A musician called Simon gives a dreadful performance of a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: Simon Rattle conducted the City of Birmingham Symphony and Berlin Philharmonic orchestras.
explanation.definitionFit: To recite a list quickly and fluently is to go through it at speed, which the phrasal verb describes.

clue.text: see 25dn.
(& 26dn./11ac.) What the PM should do: escalate Article – a flowery way, perhaps to deceive

blocks.note: a prime minister is supposed to lead the country
to escalate is to go up
the is the definite article
a path through a garden is a way lined with flowers

explanation.surface: A jibe that the prime minister, instead of leading, will escalate matters by citing an Article and use flowery talk to mislead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests Article 50 of Brexit, but it is just the grammatical word.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to mislead someone by encouraging a false belief, which is to fool or trick them.

clue.text: see 10ac.
Groping Evita's tits – just the sort of thing Trump would love

definitions.text: just the sort of thing Trump would love

indicators.note: groping hands paw and move around, so the letters are pushed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A satirical jab at Trump's known groping, imagining him with Eva Perón.
explanation.walkthrough: Trump made a much-debated state visit to the UK, which the definition alludes to.
explanation.definitionFit: An official visit by a head of state, with royal pomp and banquets, would flatter a vain president.

clue.text: (& 28ac.) Persuade Trump's no. 1 Klan organisation to, on crushing independent

indicators.note: number one is the first, so only Trump's opening letter is used
organising things means arranging them afresh, so the letters of Klan are reordered
crushing something means pressing round it, so the rearranged letters squeeze around the extra one

blocks.note: the first letter of Trump
taken as written, to be rearranged
I is the standard abbreviation for independent
taken as written

explanation.surface: A satirical claim that Trump's first move is to get the Ku Klux Klan to crush independent voices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' says the last word follows the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring someone round to doing something by argument is to convince them, the phrasal verb's meaning.

clue.text: One crappy beer in Coldstream Guards starts to be an obstacle

indicators.note: something crappy is badly made, so the word beer is mangled into a new order
starts are beginnings, so the first letter of each of Coldstream and Guards is taken
in places the jumbled beer inside the two regimental initials

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
first letter of Coldstream
taken as written, to be rearranged
first letter of Guards

explanation.surface: A soldier's bad pint in the Coldstream Guards (a British Army regiment) becomes a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: The Coldstream Guards are a foot regiment of the British Army; 'cold' in the name nods at the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge floating mass of ice is a hazard to ships, the archetypal thing that blocks a vessel's path.

clue.text: Who'd plot against Trump's spokesman (about to be replaced, by right)

indicators.note: replacing one thing by another swaps them, so one letter of the spokesman's name is exchanged

blocks.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
Sean Spicer was Trump's first White House press secretary
c (circa) means about
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone scheming against Trump's press secretary, who is soon to be replaced by a right-winger.
explanation.walkthrough: Spicer resigned after six months, so 'about to be replaced' was topical before it is mechanical.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who joins a secret scheme to do harm is a plotter, so the noun fits one who would plot.

clue.text: Sign of, for example, kicking out a member – Watson?

indicators.note: kicking something out removes it, so one letter is taken away

blocks.note: say means for example
the letter thrown out
a Member of Parliament
Tom Watson was Labour's deputy leader

explanation.surface: Asks whether Labour expelling a member is a sign of trouble under Tom Watson.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks Watson as one example of a Tom; Tom Watson was deputy leader of the UK Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A feature showing that a condition exists, especially an illness, is an indication or signal of it.

clue.text: Screw with not a care and think nothing of it

blocks.note: screw is British slang for wages
no means not a, as in no fool
to mind is to care

explanation.surface: Having casual sex without worrying about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screw' reads as sex, but in British slang it also means a wage.
explanation.definitionFit: To disregard something and not let it bother you is to ignore it, which is the idiom's sense.

clue.text: Let go of Conservative leader abandoning relative "remainer"

indicators.note: a leader stands at the front, so the first letter of Conservative is the one meant
abandoning something means leaving it behind, so that letter drops out of the relative

blocks.note: first letter of Conservative
an uncle is a relative
ash is what remains after a fire

explanation.surface: A Tory leader turning against a Remain-voting relative over Brexit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remainer' suggests a Brexit Remain voter, but it means what is left over: the ash after burning.
explanation.definitionFit: To unleash something is to release it from restraint, freeing it as a dog is freed from its lead.

clue.text: One who undoes Donald's no. 1 in 'recuse' fiasco

indicators.note: number one means the first, so only Donald's opening letter is used
a fiasco is a mess, so the word recuse ends up scrambled
in puts the single letter inside the scrambled word

blocks.note: first letter of Donald
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Trump as the man whose recusal fiasco brings someone down.
explanation.walkthrough: Recuse alludes to Jeff Sessions recusing himself from the Russia inquiry; 'undoes' means both ruins and undresses.
explanation.definitionFit: A seducer leads someone astray and, literally, gets their clothes off, so he undoes them in both senses.

clue.text: Soft screw with Dicky, which produces a winner

blocks.note: p (piano) means soft in music
lay is slang for having sex
dicky is British slang for unwell or unreliable, so off

explanation.surface: An impotence joke about a limp encounter with someone called Dicky.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky looks like a name; in British slang it means feeble or out of order.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra match played to settle a tie decides who takes the title, so its purpose is to decide the champion.

clue.text: Clear out before Brenda turns over intricate plot man

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered here, so the letters of clear are thrown into a new order
turning something over flips it end to end, so Brenda's letters run the other way

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Clearing out before the Queen discovers an elaborate conspiracy.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's long-running nickname for Queen Elizabeth II, giving ER.
explanation.definitionFit: John le Carré wrote spy novels famous for complicated storylines, so he is a writer of intricate plots.

clue.text: see 25dn.
One erection: pound (which isn't very nice)

definitions.note: a clause standing for the adjective

indicators.note: an erection raises things upward, and in a down entry going up means reading backwards

blocks.note: an means one
a pound is an enclosure for animals, like a pigsty

explanation.surface: A smutty one-liner about a single erection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Erection' sounds rude but just tells the solver to write one piece upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nasty is unpleasant or disagreeable, so it is far from nice.

clue.text: Crown had crazy American tweets galore

indicators.note: crazy means wildly disordered, so the letters of crown had are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
US is short for American

explanation.surface: The Queen's reaction to an unhinged American president's flood of tweets.
explanation.walkthrough: The tweets look like Trump's, but they are birdsong.
explanation.definitionFit: Early in the morning many birds sing together, so there are countless chirps at sunrise.

clue.text: (& 22ac./9dn.) Eagerly accompanied by Frank, member wanting 'seconds'

blocks.note: with means accompanied by
frank means open, candid
an arm is a limb, or member
s is the abbreviation for seconds

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly accompanied by a man called Frank whose member wants second helpings.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a name and member like a body part joke; they are a synonym and a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Welcoming someone warmly and enthusiastically is greeting them as if ready to embrace, which is eagerness.

clue.text: see 10ac.
POTUS gets mad with core Republican attorney

indicators.note: something mad is deranged, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: The President of the United States rages alongside a hardline Republican lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Core' looks like an instruction to take middle letters, but it is used whole.
explanation.definitionFit: An attorney is a lawyer, and one who conducts the case against a defendant is a lawyer for the state.

clue.text: see 13ac.
Greek University: "your vulgar English – it's full of holes!"

blocks.note: Gr is the abbreviation for Greek
U is the abbreviation for university
yer is a coarse, slangy spelling of your
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A Greek academic sneers at someone's crude English, calling it full of holes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Full of holes' seems to criticise the English; it is the cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruyère is a Swiss cheese popularly pictured with holes, though the classic holey cheese is really Emmental.

clue.text: Decline to enter disgusting arse for money

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece sits within the other
disgusting implies something foul and messed up, so the letters of arse are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
to decline is to die away

explanation.surface: Refusing to do something revolting to someone's backside in exchange for cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Readies is British slang for ready cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready money is cash available to spend at once, shortened in British slang to a plural noun for banknotes.
